key_insight: PathVU shows that current multimodal LLMs still struggle with fine-grained, multiscale understanding of pathology images, even when they perform well on higher-level outputs like reports or diagnoses.
clinical_relevance: Better evaluation of visual reasoning in pathology could support more reliable AI tools for assisting pathology workflows, but these models are not yet robust for detailed image interpretation.
method: Built a vision-anchored benchmark from 23 public pathology datasets with human-supervised labels and spatial annotations.
Tested two fields of view: Region FOV for local high-resolution regions and Slide FOV for whole-slide views.
Converted annotations into deterministic targets for tasks such as localization, recognition, counting, spatial reasoning, and insufficient-context judgment.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 14 VQA-style tasks, 61,673 images, 308,070 samples, 28 organs, and 7,253,526 annotations, and it was used to evaluate 18 representative MLLMs.
watch_item: Results depend on benchmark annotation quality and task design, so strong performance on PathVU may not fully capture real-world pathology workflow reliability.
paper_title: PathView-Bench: Can Multimodal Large Language Models Achieve Fine-grained Multiscale Understanding of Pathology Images?
